sub_graphs.title: Cancun ECRECOVER: Signature Recovery Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the runtime behavior of the ecrecover precompiled contract for ECDSA signature recovery

nodes.label: ECRECOVER Precompile Called
nodes.description: Contract call to address 0x01 with signature data

nodes.label: Parse Input Data
nodes.description: Extract 128 bytes: hash (32), v (32), r (32), s (32)

nodes.label: Input Data Parsed
nodes.description: Signature components extracted and ready for validation

nodes.label: Validate Recovery ID v
nodes.description: Check v is exactly 27 or 28

nodes.label: Invalid v Value
nodes.description: v not in {27, 28}, return empty output

nodes.label: Validate r Parameter
nodes.description: Check 0 < r < SECP256K1N

nodes.label: Invalid r Value
nodes.description: r out of range, return empty output

nodes.label: Validate s Parameter
nodes.description: Check 0 < s < SECP256K1N

nodes.label: Invalid s Value
nodes.description: s out of range, return empty output

nodes.label: All Parameters Valid
nodes.description: v, r, s all within valid ranges

nodes.label: Recover Public Key
nodes.description: Call secp256k1_recover(r, s, v-27, hash) to derive public key

nodes.label: Key Recovery Failed
nodes.description: InvalidSignatureError caught, return empty output

nodes.label: Public Key Recovered
nodes.description: secp256k1 public key successfully derived from signature

nodes.label: Derive Ethereum Address
nodes.description: Keccak-256 hash of public key, take last 20 bytes

nodes.label: Pad Address to 32 Bytes
nodes.description: Left-pad 20-byte address with 12 zero bytes

nodes.label: ECRECOVER Success
nodes.description: 32-byte padded address returned to caller

nodes.label: ECRECOVER Empty Return
nodes.description: No output returned due to invalid input or recovery failure

ambiguities.text: The specification does not clarify behavior when input is shorter than 128 bytes
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume input is right-padded with zeros to 128 bytes, as is standard for precompile input handling

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly address EIP-2 low-s normalization
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume ecrecover accepts both low-s and high-s signatures per historical behavior, but callers should use low-s for compatibility

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot forge ECDSA signatures without knowing the private key
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Complete compromise of signature-based authentication in all Ethereum contracts

implicit_assumptions.description: The secp256k1_recover implementation is correct and resistant to timing attacks
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Side-channel attacks could leak private key information

implicit_assumptions.description: Callers understand that ecrecover returns address(0) for invalid signatures rather than reverting
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts may incorrectly accept actions from address(0) if not checking return value
